question: Should OpenClaw continue supporting or backporting the legacy `skills/skill-creator/scripts/init_skill.py --resources` helper now that current main routes durable skill creation through `skill_workshop`?
rationale: Automation can prove the latest stable release has the old case-sensitive parser and the linked PR fixes it, but current main removed the helper and current skill-creator guidance points to a different product surface.

options.title: Close obsolete helper cluster
options.body: Close the linked PR and this issue together with evidence that current main no longer supports `init_skill.py` and `skill_workshop` is the supported skill-creation path.

options.title: Refresh and land helper repair
options.body: Ask for or create a refreshed PR that intentionally restores or maintains `init_skill.py`, adds the mixed-case parser tests, and explains the supported release/backport story.

options.title: Backport only
options.body: Keep current main as-is but prepare a release-branch-only fix if maintainers consider the shipped helper a supported contract for `v2026.6.11` users.

recommendation.title: Close obsolete helper cluster
recommendation.body: Close the linked PR and this issue together with evidence that current main no longer supports `init_skill.py` and `skill_workshop` is the supported skill-creation path.

likelyOwner.reason: The original bundled skill surface was introduced by Peter Steinberger, and this is primarily a product-boundary choice about the old helper versus the current skill-workshop path.
